title: Finite discrete condensed coefficients and ordinary module sheaves
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with its discrete condensed structure $\underline A$, and let $T$ be a scheme. Work on the small pro-étale site with the size and sheafification conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The pulled-back ring object $p_T^*\underline A$ is isomorphic, as a ring object, to the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. The section-action equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] gives an exact equivalence between internal $p_T^*\underline A$-module objects and ordinary $A_T$-module sheaves. Its termwise extension is an equivalence of unbounded derived categories preserving relative derived tensor products and every Tor-amplitude interval [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. It identifies the finite constant local models and bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and preserves shifts, distinguished triangles, and small coproducts, hence their localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ of $f$, these equivalences identify the module-object composite $Rp_*D(j_!)$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] with the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf composite $Rp_*j_!$ for that same compactification [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification].

source.place: Step 8, coefficient identification and exact derived equivalence between internal module objects and ordinary constant-ring sheaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] with $B=A$, then [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] with $T$. The first gives a ring-object isomorphism $a(\underline A_{\mathrm{pre}})\cong\underline A$ at the profinite point; the second pulls it to $c_T:A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}p_T^*\underline A$. Both statements allow the zero ring and the empty scheme. The universe lift in their constant presheaves is the scalar-universe encoding of $A$, so it does not change the ring. Use this one canonical family $c_T$ throughout.

source.place: Section 5.3 as context; constant-sheaf adjunction argument of the cited ring-identification nodes (not an etale/pro-etale derived comparison)

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] on the fixed small pro-etale site. Its size and monoidal-sheafification hypotheses are precisely those imposed in the statement. Restrict scalars through $c_T$ to obtain an equivalence $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{p_T^*\underline A}\to\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)$. In section coordinates it sends an action $\gamma$ to $a\cdot m=\gamma_U(c_T(a)\otimes m)$ and sends a module morphism to the identical homomorphism of underlying abelian sheaves. The inverse uses $c_T^{-1}$ in the same formula. Thus $E_T$ and its inverse are additive. Since inverse equivalences preserve the universal properties of kernels and cokernels, they preserve exact sequences. In particular $H^n(E_TK)=E_T H^n(K)$.

source.place: Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi); the cited section-action equivalence and its explicit scalar change

proof.text: The ordinary category may also be written $\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Mod}_A)$. An $A_T$-action restricts to an $A$-action on every section group. Conversely a sheaf of $A$-modules has an $A_T$-action: a section of $A_T$ is locally represented by a constant scalar, which acts on that member of the cover, and these products glue uniquely. The two procedures are inverse since equality of sheaf maps is local. This identifies the ordinary section-ring and fixed-$A$ coefficient descriptions used in the compact-support clause, including their morphisms.

source.place: Constant scalar sheaves and sectionwise module actions; explicit gluing argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to $E_T$ and its exact inverse. Their unit and counit apply termwise and descend through quasi-isomorphisms, yielding inverse equivalences $D(E_T)$ of the unbounded derived categories. The cited theorem supplies compatibility with shifts and distinguished triangles. The cohomology identity of step 2 shows that $D(E_T)$ preserves and reflects every cohomological vanishing interval, with no boundedness assumption on the input.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, and localization at quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] with $C=T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ and $R=p_T^*\underline A$; its site, sheafification and closed-monoidal hypotheses are exactly those used in step 2 and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. It gives natural isomorphisms $E_R(M\otimes_RN)\cong E_RM\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}E_RN$ and $E_R(R)\cong R_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for the coequalizer tensor of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] and the sheafified balanced tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], given on local pure tensors by $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$ and compatible with associators, unitors and symmetry. By step 2, $E_T$ is $E_R$ followed by restriction of scalars along the ring-sheaf isomorphism $c_T:A_T\to R_{\mathrm{sec}}$. Under $c_T$ the balancing relations $m a\otimes n=m\otimes an$ over $R_{\mathrm{sec}}(U)$ and over $A_T(U)$ are the same relations, so the presheaf tensors of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] coincide sectionwise and hence after sheafification, with the same action through the first factor. Composing gives the natural, coherent comparison $E_T(M\otimes_{p_T^*\underline A}N)\cong E_TM\otimes_{A_T}E_TN$ with $E_T(p_T^*\underline A)\cong A_T$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (sheafified balanced tensor); comparison supplied by the cited internal/section tensor node

proof.text: Both equivalences preserve small coproducts: for a family $(M_i)$ and any $L$, the equivalence identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(E_T(\bigoplus_i M_i),L)$ with $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(E_TM_i,L)$, the coproduct universal property. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], $E_R$ applied termwise identifies the direct-sum total tensor complexes, with differential $d(m\otimes n)=dm\otimes n+(-1)^{\deg m}m\otimes dn$, and preserves and reflects acyclicity and K-flat complexes in the acyclic-total-tensor sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex]; restricting scalars along $c_T$ as in step 5 changes none of this. The internal K-flatness of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] is [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] ($P\otimes-$ and $-\otimes P$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms), which is the same test: the additive total tensor commutes with mapping cones, a map is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when its cone is acyclic, $0\to Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when $Q$ is acyclic, and the symmetry handles the second side. Hence an internal K-flat resolution $P\to K$ goes to an ordinary K-flat resolution $E_TP\to E_TK$. Computing [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-derived-tensor] on this same $P$ gives the natural comparison $D(E_T)(K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{p_T^*\underline A}L)\cong D(E_T)K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{A}D(E_T)L$.

source.place: K-flat computation of derived tensor, with the explicit acyclic-test argument; definitions in the cited tensor nodes

proof.text: Every ordinary module sheaf in degree zero is the image of an internal module sheaf in degree zero, and conversely. For each such test $N$, steps 2 and 6 identify $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathrm L}N)$ with its image under the exact equivalence. Since the equivalence reflects zero objects, the vanishing tests in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] are equivalent for every integer $i$ and every $N$. This proves preservation and reflection of each specified interval $[a,b]$, not merely existence of some finite interval.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude; comparison of identical tensor tests

proof.text: The coefficient family in step 1 is compatible with pullback: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-coefficient-sections] says that its section maps commute with the direct-image coefficient map for every scheme morphism and every test object. For $h:U\to T$, write $b_h:h^{-1}A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_U$ for the canonical constant-sheaf map. The cited section equation says $\eta_h c_T=(h_*c_U)\eta_h^{\mathrm{const}}$. Taking adjoint transposes gives $c_U b_h=\alpha_h(h^{-1}c_T)$, an equality of maps $h^{-1}A_T\to p_U^*\underline A$. In the formulas of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], both pullbacks are the inverse-image abelian sheaf with scalars extended along this same ring map. Using the balanced tensor comparison of step 5 gives $E_Uh^*\cong h^*E_T$. This applies to every covering map and locally closed stratum, with no finiteness or smoothness condition on $h$.

source.place: Ringed-topos pullback formula; coefficient-section compatibility from the cited node, using Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 5.4.1 only as geometric context

proof.text: For a finitely presented $A$-module $P$, choose a finite presentation $A^r\xrightarrow{B}A^s\to P\to0$ with scalar matrix $B$. By steps 2, 5 and 8 the local model $(p_U^*\underline A)\otimes_A P$ is sent to the cokernel of the identical matrix $A_U^r\xrightarrow{B}A_U^s$, namely the constant module sheaf $P_U$: the constant presheaf has this cokernel objectwise, and sheafification preserves its cokernel universal property by its left adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Conversely the inverse equivalence uses the identical presentation. Thus the same pro-etale cover trivializes the model in either description. Applying this on the same constructible locally closed strata proves equivalence of the constructibility predicates in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], on qcqs schemes and affine-locally on arbitrary schemes. Step 4 handles bounded cohomology and step 7 handles the Tor interval, so $D(E_T)$ identifies their bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories. Finite $A$ makes every finitely presented $P$ finite; conversely a finite module over the finite ring $A$ has a finite presentation, since the kernel of a finite free surjection is a finite set and therefore finitely generated.

source.place: Coefficient identification in the parent split, step 8; explicit finite-presentation argument

proof.text: An equivalence of derived categories preserves small coproducts by the same Hom universal-property calculation as in step 6. Together with step 4 it therefore carries replete triangulated coproduct-closed subcategories to subcategories with those properties. If such a subcategory on the ordinary side contains the ordinary bounded constructible finite-Tor objects, its inverse image contains the internal ones by step 9. Intersecting all these subcategories, as in [sk-def-localizing-closure], gives one inclusion between the localizing closures. Applying the same argument to the inverse equivalence gives the opposite inclusion. Thus the equivalence restricts to the asserted localizing closures. The intersection definition of [sk-def-localizing-closure] is stated there for $A$ annihilated by a power of $\ell$, the case used by the parent; the same intersection makes sense verbatim for any finite $A$, and the argument uses nothing about $\ell$.

source.place: Parent split step 8; universal definition of localizing closure

proof.text: For $h:U\to T$, both underived direct images have section group $M(V\times_TU)$ on $V\in T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]; [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and, through step 3, [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]). In the internal construction the scalar acts through $\eta_h$; in the ordinary construction it acts through the constant-ring restriction. The equation in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-coefficient-sections] identifies these actions, so the identity on the section groups gives a natural isomorphism $E_Th_*\cong h_*E_U$. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, step 8 identifies internal $j^*$ with the ordinary module pullback, which for an open immersion is restriction $(j^*G)(W\to U)=G(W\to U\to T)$, the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction] read through step 3. The exact internal $j_!$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and the ordinary $j_!$ of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero] (the one used in [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification]) are both left adjoint to these, by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. They are therefore identified by their Hom bijections: $\operatorname{Hom}(E_Tj_!M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*E_T^{-1}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E_UM,j^*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!E_UM,N)$. The bijections are natural and their identity transposes give inverse isomorphisms.

source.place: Module pushforward and adjunction with open restriction; the section-action equality and explicit adjoint Hom bijections

proof.text: The exact equivalences $E_U,E_T$ preserve K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since each is right adjoint to its exact inverse. Given any complex $M$ on $U$, choose an internal K-injective resolution $M\to I$. Then $E_UM\to E_UI$ is an ordinary K-injective resolution. Compute the two derived direct images on these representatives: step 11 gives $E_T(h_*I)\cong h_*(E_UI)$ termwise, hence $D(E_T)Rh_*\cong Rh_*D(E_U)$ naturally on the unbounded categories, using [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The exact $j_!$ comparison from step 11 applies termwise. For the fixed compactification $c=(j,p)$, compose these two comparisons to obtain $D(E_Y)Rp_*D(j_!)\cong Rp_*j_!D(E_X)$. These are exactly the two composites defined in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification]. No compactification change or etale/pro-etale comparison is used.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; K-injective computation of the separately derived compactification factors

lean.statement: theorem moduleObject_ordinary_coefficient_equivalence [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A] : ∃ E : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Encoding A T, (∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Nonempty ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.Monoidal) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b → (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude T A ((E T).ordinaryDerived.functor.obj K) a b)) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b → (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K))) ∧ (∀ M : Internal A T, HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (coefficient A) T M ↔ ordinaryLocalModel A T (((E T).ordinary.functor ⋙ (E T).fixed.functor).obj M)) ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T), (constantModelBoundedConstructible (coefficient A) T K ∧ DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ K) ↔ ordinaryCtf A T ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K)) ∧ Nonempty ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.CommShift ℤ) ∧ (E T).fixedDerived.functor.IsTriangulated ∧ PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (E T).fixedDerived.functor ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T), localizingClosureProEtale (coefficient A) T K ↔ CategoryTheory.localizingClosure (ordinaryCtf A T) ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K))) ∧ (∀ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : Compactification f), Nonempty (CondensedRing.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (coefficient A) c ⋙ (E Y).fixedDerived.functor ≅ (E X).fixedDerived.functor ⋙ rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)) c))
lean.note: The canonical coefficient map is sheafified constant functions followed by the existing constantSchemeIso and upperStarFromPoint. Encoding fixes the ring isomorphism on every constant scalar and fixes both forward functors to section-action/scalar restriction. Its two derived equivalences are the actual termwise Equivalence.mapDerivedCategory, not independent equivalences. Tensor and compactification comparison use the equivalent fixed-ULift-A module-sheaf presentation; Tor intervals are also compared directly with the recorded intrinsic HasProEtaleTorAmplitude. The ordinary local-model and constructibility helpers render the ordinary side of this node with the same covers, strata and affine-local convention; they introduce no new independent notion or chosen data. The two definition nodes def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction and def-sfb-constant-sheaf-scheme-pullback-comparison own the existing canonical constructions used by the signature; the associated theorem nodes are proof dependencies. The recorded derived-constant-module interface is also a statement dependency.
